chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: Music Town's staff, Norman Siminoff and the program
summary: The program for An American Rhapsody lists dance directors, drama teacher Laura Bowman, and Sheffield as public relations, with photography by Norman Siminoff and wartime ads.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And also on your staff there, you also had Malcolm Nash, dance director; Archie Savage, dance director; Laura Bowman, dramatic arts. She came out of the Lafayette Players.
And Horace Willard, radio technique and recording. Oh, here--CBS, it says. You said he was associated with one of the studios. And Maceo B. Sheffield, public relations.
Heh heh heh. I had to put him down as somethin'.
And Norman Siminoff, photography, and Dewey L. Johnson, radio productions. You told me earlier today that Norman Siminoff was a Jewish fellow who taught Sheffield photography. Is that right?

Yeah, I guess he...they came there as partners, and I know Simi had been a photographer long time. I know him on the Avenue. Then when he and Sheffield come out there, he done nearly all the work so I know that Sheffield was learnin' from him.
And you said Simi was the one who put together this program and did all the artwork. Right?
Well, all the handwork in there nearly, you know, he...he was good at that.
And it was at...and you've got an ad in here for Ivie's Chicken Shack, 1105 1/2 East Vernon, an ad from Lena Horne and Ethel Waters and Hattie McDaniel and Eddie Anderson and...
Count Basie and 'The People's Voice', America's Greatest Negro Newspaper.'
Well, that was a war worker. He's been dead, I think, a long time. They were up on uh...it {came} out during the war.
